description: Create a new connection using the provided payload.

connection_payload.description: The configuration payload for the connection. Canonical fields include ``provider``, ``name``, ``description``, ``parameters``, ``enabled``, ``createdByUser``, and ``supportedModelTypes``.

examples.user_query: Create a new connection for the sales database.
examples.notes: This call creates a connection to the sales database hosted on a PostgreSQL server. Use this when setting up data sources for analytics.

examples.user_query: Set up a connection to the marketing analytics data warehouse.
examples.notes: This call establishes a connection to a Snowflake data warehouse for marketing analytics. Use this for querying and analyzing marketing data.

examples.user_query: Add a connection to the customer support database.
examples.notes: This call sets up a connection to a MySQL database containing customer support data. Use this for integrating support data into dashboards.

description: Generate a connection payload for a given data source type.

datasource_type.description: Type of data source. One of ``"Athena"``, ``"RedShift"``, ``"BigQuery"``, ``"DataBricks"`` (case-insensitive).

connection_params.description: Connection details. Supported keys depend on ``datasource_type``: - Athena: ``name`` (required), ``region`` (required), ``s3_output_location`` (required), ``aws_access_key`` (required), ``aws_secret_key`` (required), ``description``, ``schema``, ``additional_parameters``. - DataBricks: ``name`` (required), ``connection_string`` (required), ``token`` (required), ``description``, ``use_dynamic_schema``, ``schema``. - BigQuery: ``name`` (required), ``service_account_key_path`` (required), ``description``, ``use_service_account``, ``use_proxy_server``, ``use_dynamic_schema``, ``record_field_flattening_level``, ``unnest_arrays``, ``allow_large_results``, ``use_storage_api``, ``additional_parameters``, ``database``. - RedShift: ``server`` (required), ``username`` (required), ``password`` (required), ``name``, ``description``, ``default_database``, ``additional_parameters``.

examples.user_query: How can I generate a connections payload for an Athena datasource?
examples.notes: This call generates a connections payload for an Athena datasource, specifying the AWS region, database name, and S3 output location.

examples.user_query: I need to prepare a connections payload for a Snowflake datasource. How do I do that?
examples.notes: This call generates a connections payload for a Snowflake datasource, including details like account URL, warehouse, database, and schema.

examples.user_query: What is the payload for connecting to an Oracle database?
examples.notes: This call generates a connections payload for an Oracle database, providing the host, port, service name, and credentials.

connection_name.description: Name of the connection to filter by.

examples.notes: This retrieves the connection details for 'FinanceCluster', which might be used for financial data analysis or reporting.

examples.notes: This call retrieves a list of all data connections configured in the Sisense instance. Use it to review available connections.

connection_data.description: Fields to update (for example ``name``, ``parameters``, ``provider``). Supported keys depend on the Sisense connection type.

examples.user_query: How can I update the name and parameters of an existing connection?
examples.notes: This call updates the name and connection parameters for the specified connection. Use this when migrating to a new database host.

examples.user_query: I need to change the provider of a connection. How do I do that?
examples.notes: This call changes the provider for the specified connection. Use this when switching to a different data source type.

examples.user_query: Can I update multiple fields of a connection at once?
examples.notes: This call updates multiple fields of the specified connection, including name, parameters, and provider. Use this for comprehensive updates during migrations or reconfigurations.
